newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia launches search after East Timor ambush.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia launches search after East Timor ambush.

text.p: Indonesian soldiers have launched a search for East Timorese guerrillas who killed a senior government official, an aide and four security guards in an ambush in the territory, a military official said on Thursday.

"We have launched a search to capture them. Four platoons of troops have been deployed in Viqueque to find the rebels," the official told Reuters by telephone from Dili, the capital of troubled East Timor.

The official, who declined to be identified, said at least five people were wounded in the attack and in another ambush on Monday at a village near Viqueque town, some 120 km (75 miles) south of Dili.
"We believe there are 15 of them who conducted the attack and their rifles include M-16s. The rebels stole the rifles from military posts," he said.
The official declined to give further details but said Viqueque was calm on Thursday and there were no fresh attacks overnight.

The military has said one of the victims was Eugenio da Costa, the head of the Viqueque regency's administrative affairs department. It said the others killed included another government official and four of da Costa's bodyguards.

The military said the attackers fired at a pickup truck da Costa was driving. The vehicle spun out of control into a ditch and at least one of the victims died of stab wounds, indicating the rebels then attacked the survivors, it said.
Three occupants of the pickup escaped but were wounded, the military said.
Later, the guerrillas ambushed another vehicle in the same area, wounding three employees of a company working on a development project in the region.
Military officials have in the past said the number of armed rebels in East Timor is dwindling and that they do not number more than 200 poorly equipped fighters.

Reported attacks by the rebels are rare. The Viqueque ambush comes more than one year after the killing of two people in Ermera regency, 65 km (40 miles) south of Dili. That attack, in January 1996, was blamed on the guerrillas.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which still considers former colonial ruler Portugal as the administering power.
